newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia Jan-April gov't deficit at 1.78 pct GDP.
newsitem.headline: Colombia Jan-April gov't deficit at 1.78 pct GDP.

text.p: Colombia's central government fiscal deficit for the four months January to April stood at 1.78 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) compared with 1.39 percent of GDP in the same period last year, the Finance Ministry said in a statement Tuesday.

The widening central government deficit was due to a smaller increase in total income, which rose just 13.3 percent in the first four months of this year compared with the same period last year. Government income rose 39.6 percent in the first four months of 1996 against the same period in 1995.
Government expenditure for the first four months of the year rose 26.9 percent to 1.99 trillion pesos compared with January-April 1996, when expenditure hit 1.24 trillion pesos.

Much of the shortfall in income was due to the slowdown in tax revenues, which rose 14.4 percent in the January to April period compared with the first four months of last year. Tax revenues rose 34.4 percent in the first four months of 1996 compared with the same period in 1995. The slowdown in tax revenues is largely seen as a consequence of the poor performance of the Colombian economy last year, when GDP grew just 2.01 percent, one of the lowest rates in a decade.
Colombian businesses pay tax bills in five installments based on their previous year's income.
In the first four months of this year the government paid out a total of 830 billion pesos to service domestic and foreign debt compared with 623 billion pesos in the same period last year.
